set.body:
align/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/align/source.scala:252

  def relativePosition(ref: SourceNodeRef): Double =
    relativeSpan(ref).map((a, b) => (a + b) / 2.0).getOrElse(0.0)

relativeSpan is correctly fail-closed: it returns None when the ref has no node in this
view, or when textLength is 0. relativePosition then converts that None into 0.0, which
is not a missing marker -- it is a MEANINGFUL POSITION, the very start of the discourse.

The laundering is at signature.scala:392 and population.scala:271, which are identical:

  val discoursePos: SourceNodeRef => Option[Double] = r => Some(view.relativePosition(r))

The declared type carries an absence channel. The implementation makes None structurally
unreachable. On the LINE BELOW, in both files, worldPos uses the same channel correctly:

  view.worldOrder.map(o => r => o.get(r).map(_.toDouble))

So the absence channel is understood and used properly for world order, and hardcoded
shut for discourse position, in adjacent lines.

WHY THIS IS NOT SPECULATIVE: signature.scala:395-396 carries this comment --
"ordered already abstains when no step carries directional mass; the previous
.getOrElse(1.0) threw that away and published PERFECT forward chronology for a recall
we [could not measure]". The identical fail-open was already found and fixed ONCE in
this function. The fix landed on `ordered` and did not look three lines up.

REACHABILITY IS UNMEASURED AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT. Two paths reach the getOrElse:
textLength == 0 (searched; no construction with a literal 0 found, so this looks
unreachable today) and node(ref) == None (unmeasured). Evidence someone thought the ref
could miss: embed-bench/metrics.scala:340 and :369 both guard the call as
view.node(ref).map(_ => view.relativePosition(ref)) -- a consumer defending against
exactly the condition the core path swallows.

PROMOTION CRITERION: if a ref reaching signature.scala:392 or population.scala:271 can
be absent from the view, this is P1 -- those feed the discourse-position channel of the
signature, and chronology is the number that moved 2.6x in the d_ent experiment. Measure
that BEFORE fixing. If it is unreachable, fix the type anyway and say so in the commit:
an Option that cannot be None is a false declaration whether or not today's callers trip
it, and the next caller inherits the lie.

DO NOT fix by threading Option through blindly -- consumers currently receive a total
function. Establish reachability first, then decide whether the fix is at the type or at
the call sites.
set.title: relativePosition destroys absence, and two call sites wrap it in an Option that can never be None
